title: Pairwise ranking evaluation framework for customer promptsets + A/B hooks
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a lightweight, production-safe evaluation harness that captures pairwise and listwise ranking metrics (NDCG@k and MRR) on customer prompt sets and wires A/B-test hooks into the inference path. The goal is to provide per-customer, per-model signals for rank quality without adding >5ms p50 latency to the online reranking path, and to enable reliable offline/online comparison across model variants and quantization profiles.
context_and_motivation: We currently lack a consistent signal tied to customer prompt sets for reranking quality. Several customers have reported regressions after model variant rollouts; existing metrics are coarse and not tied to prompt distributions. This ticket creates an opinionated evaluation pipeline and lightweight runtime instrumentation to correlate offline NDCG/MRR with online A/B outcomes and latency/cost trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible pipeline that ingests customer prompt sets (CSV/JSONL) and computes NDCG@1/3/5 and MRR per promptset and per-model variant
Runtime A/B hook that samples 1-5% of live rerank requests and attaches anonymized evaluation context to events without leaking PII
Telemetry dashboards showing daily NDCG/MRR trends, per-model deltas, and sample-level failure rates
End-to-end test demonstrating <5ms median added latency for the A/B hook on a representative request mix
Docs and runbook for interpreting rank deltas and abort thresholds for rollouts (e.g., automatic rollback if NDCG drop > 2.5% and customer_impact high)
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Product and Observability. Agreed scope: pairwise comparator first, listwise later. Decided to reuse existing embeddings ingest lambda for promptset plumbing.
2026-03-04: PoC pairwise evaluator implemented in eval-service (prototype branch). Computes pairwise win rates and MRR for small promptsets. Not yet production hardened.
2026-03-06: Perf profiling: PoC adds ~12ms p50 on local replica due to synchronous store writes. Decision: switch to buffered async writes to telemetry pipeline to meet latency SLO.
2026-03-09: Security review sync: decided to anonymize prompt IDs and strip user-identifying tokens before storing. Legal asked for retention policy — set to 30 days by default.
2026-03-10: Instrumentation PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-eval/pull/128 (WIP). Working on integration tests and dashboard wiring.
decisions: Use pairwise comparisons as primary signal for initial rollout (better for sparse relevance labels)
Store only hashed prompt identifiers and aggregate metrics in long-term storage; raw prompt text kept ephemeral (<30 days)
Sample 1-5% of live traffic for runtime A/B hooks; provide config knob per-customer for scale
Compute NDCG@1/3/5 and MRR in offline pipeline, expose deltas in Console and alerting
test_plan: Unit tests for evaluator functions (ndcg, mrr, pairwise) with edge cases (ties, empty relevance)
Load test for A/B hook path to validate <5ms added latency at 95th percentile on standard traffic mix
Integration test that ingests a sample customer promptset and verifies consistent metric outputs across branches
E2E canary: enable sampling for a low-impact customer and compare offline eval to live click-through changes over 48h
rollout_plan: Stage 0: deploy eval pipeline in staging, run historical promptsets to validate baseline values
Stage 1: enable runtime A/B hook at 0.5% sampling for internal beta customers; monitor telemetry for 72h
Stage 2: expand sampling to 2% for selected customers and enable dashboard alerts for NDCG/MRR regression
Stage 3: full rollout to all customers with opt-out and per-customer sampling controls
risks: Telemetry volume growth if promptset ingestion is unrestricted — mitigated by quota and retention defaults
Latency regressions if A/B hook synchronous path isn't fully async; will gate by perf tests
False positives from small promptsets — will surface confidence intervals and minimum sample thresholds
Potential customer privacy concerns — apply hashing and retention controls, coordinate with Legal
next_steps: Finish async buffering implementation and run perf benchmarks (assigned: Mateo)
Complete PR with integration tests and request review from Observability and Security teams
Create Console dashboard tile and link to runbook entries (owner: Product)
Schedule canary with 1 customer and collect first 48h comparison report
notes_for_reviewers: Review focus: confirm anonymization is sufficient, ensure async buffering meets reliability needs, and validate metric definitions (NDCG cutoff choices). Pay attention to storage schema to avoid accidental PII retention.
